text_en: The Emergency Alert System is introduced in the United States.
Turkey threatens Cyprus on account of a deal to buy Russian S-300 missiles, prompting the Cypriot Missile Crisis.
Murder of Ennis Cosby: Near Interstate 405 in Los Angeles, Bill Cosby's son Ennis is shot in the head in a failed robbery attempt.
A Delta II rocket carrying a military GPS payload explodes, shortly after liftoff from Cape Canaveral.
In northwest Rwanda, Hutu militia members kill 6 Spanish aid workers and three soldiers, and seriously wound another.
Yasser Arafat returns to Hebron after more than 30 years, and joins celebrations over the handover of the last Israeli-controlled West Bank city. (→ Hebron Agreement)
Madeleine Albright becomes the first female Secretary of State of the United States, after confirmation by the United States Senate.
VJTI changes its name from Victoria Jubilee Technical Institute to Veermata Jijabai Technological Institute in Mumbai.
1997 Liechtenstein general election: The Patriotic Union remains the largest party and wins a majority of 13 seats in the Landtag.
Sandline affair: Australian newspapers publish stories that the government of Papua New Guinea has brought mercenaries onto Bougainville Island.
STS-82: Tune-up and repair work on the Hubble Space Telescope is started by astronauts from the Space Shuttle Discovery.
U.S. President Bill Clinton bans federal funding for any research on human cloning.
In Sri Lanka, the Tamil Tigers overrun a military base and kill over 100 Sri Lankan troops.
American rapper The Notorious B.I.G. is murdered in Los Angeles.
Sandline affair: On Bougainville Island in Papua New Guinea, soldiers of commander Jerry Singirok arrest Tim Spicer and his mercenaries of the Sandline International.
The tail of a Russian An-24 charter plane breaks off while en route to Turkey, causing the plane to crash, killing all 50 on board, and resulting in the grounding of all An-24s.
In Zaire, Étienne Tshisekedi is appointed prime minister; he ejects supporters of Mobutu Sese Seko from his cabinet.
The Comet Hale–Bopp makes its closest approach to Earth.

The 69th Academy Awards, hosted by Billy Crystal, are held at the Shrine Auditorium in Los Angeles, with The English Patient winning Best Picture. During the event, the DVD format is launched in the United States.
26 – In San Diego, 39 Heaven's Gate cultists commit mass suicide at their compound.
Julius Chan resigns as prime minister of Papua New Guinea, effectively ending the Sandline affair.
The Thalit massacre in Algeria: all but 1 of the 53 inhabitants of Thalit are killed by guerrillas.
The Red River of the North breaks through dikes and floods Grand Forks, North Dakota, and East Grand Forks, Minnesota, causing US$2 billion in damage.
A Pegasus rocket carries the remains of 24 people into earth orbit, in the first space burial by Celestis company.
42 villagers are killed in the Omaria massacre in Algeria.
Tony Blair becomes Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, as the Labour Party wins the 1997 United Kingdom general election and returns to government for the first time in 18 years.
The 7.3 Mw Qayen earthquake strikes eastern Iran with a maximum Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme). At least 1,567 were killed and 2,300 were injured.
IBM's Deep Blue defeats Garry Kasparov in the last game of the rematch, the first time a computer beats a chess World champion in a match.
The United States government acknowledges existence of the "Secret War" in Laos (1953–1975) during the Vietnam War, and dedicates the Laos Memorial in honor of Hmong and other "Secret War" veterans.
Troops of Laurent Kabila march into Kinshasa.
Radiohead releases OK Computer
A military coup in Sierra Leone replaces President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah with Major Johnny Paul Koroma.
The fourth-deadliest tornado of the 1990s hits in Jarrell, Texas, killing 27 people and causing extreme damage in the Double Creek Estates.
The 13-kilometer Confederation Bridge, the world's longest bridge spanning ice-covered waters, opens between Prince Edward Island and New Brunswick, Canada.
In Denver, Colorado, Timothy McVeigh is convicted on 15 counts of murder and conspiracy for his role in the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing.
Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot orders the killing of his defense chief, Son Sen, and 11 of Sen's family members, before Pol Pot flees his northern stronghold.
In the United Kingdom, the House of Commons votes for a total ban on handguns.
A jury sentences Timothy McVeigh to death for his part in the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing.
About 50 people are killed in the Daïat Labguer (M'sila) massacre in Algeria.
The Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA) plays its first game at The Great Western Forum in Los Angeles.
The United Kingdom hands sovereignty of the British colony in Hong Kong to the People's Republic of China.
The Bank of Thailand floats the baht, triggering the Asian financial crisis.
NASA's Pathfinder space probe lands on the surface of Mars.
NATO invites the Czech Republic, Hungary, and Poland to join the alliance in 1999.

In London, scientists report their DNA analysis findings from a Neanderthal skeleton, which support the out of Africa theory of human evolution, placing an "African Eve" at 100,000 to 200,000 years ago.
Royal Jomtien Resort Hotel fire at Pattaya, Thailand's worst hotel fire, kills 90.
The remains of Che Guevara are returned to Cuba for burial, alongside some of his comrades. Guevara and his comrades were executed on October 9 1967 in Bolivia.
Spree killer Andrew Cunanan shoots fashion designer Gianni Versace dead outside Versace's Miami Beach residence.
The F. W. Woolworth Company closes after 117 years in business.
K. R. Narayanan is sworn in as India's 10th president and the first member of the Dalit caste to hold this office.
About 50 are killed in the Si Zerrouk massacre in Algeria.
18 people are killed in the Thredbo landslide in the Snowy Mountains resort in Australia.
Between 40 and 76 villagers are killed in the Oued El-Had and Mezouara massacre in Algeria.

11 – Two of the three islands of the Union of the Comoros – Anjouan and Mohéli – attempt to revert to colonial rule by France. The plan fails when the French government of President Jacques Chirac refuses to recolonize them, resulting in the two islands being reintegrated into the Comoros over the next two years.
Jeanne Calment, the verified oldest person to have ever lived, dies at 122 years and 164 days.
Korean Air Flight 801 crash lands west of Guam International Airport, resulting in the deaths of 228 people.
Trey Parker and Matt Stone's animated television comedy series, South Park, started broadcasting with the first episode, Cartman Gets an Anal Probe, on Comedy Central.
More than 60 are killed, 15 kidnapped in the Souhane massacre in Algeria.

Death of Diana, Princess of Wales: Diana, Princess of Wales, is taken to a hospital after a car accident shortly after midnight, in the Pont de l'Alma road tunnel in Paris. She is pronounced dead at 4:00 am.
Dublin Regulation on treatment of applications for right of asylum under European Union law first comes into force.
The funeral of Diana, Princess of Wales, takes place at Westminster Abbey, London, UK, watched by over two billion people worldwide.

Scotland votes in favour of a devolved Parliament, forming the Scottish Parliament less than two years later. Television series, Melangkah di Atas Awan was aired by Indonesian private television station, Indosiar. It was a final TV series of Ryan Hidayat, who died on 8 February 1997, before the TV series was broadcast.
The Norwegian parliamentary election is held in Norway.
53 people are killed in the Guelb El-Kebir massacre in Algeria.
Luke Woodham walks into Pearl High School in Pearl, Mississippi and opens fire, killing two girls, after killing his mother earlier that morning.

British scientists Moira Bruce and John Collinge, with their colleagues, independently show that the new variant form of the Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease is the same disease as Bovine spongiform encephalopathy.
The President of Paraguay, Juan Carlos Wasmosy, orders the arrest of political opponent Lino Oviedo.
Uruguay's worst air disaster occurs when Austral Líneas Aéreas Flight 2553 crashes near Nuevo Berlín, killing all 74 on board.
Sidi Daoud massacre: 43 are killed at a false roadblock in Algeria.
The first color photograph appears on the front page of The New York Times.

The remains of Che Guevara are laid to rest with full military honours in a specially built mausoleum in the city of Santa Clara, Cuba, where he had won the decisive battle of the Cuban Revolution 39 years before.
Danish escaped criminal Steen Christensen robs the Hotel Palace in Helsinki, Finland, killing two police officers while evading capture.
Iraq disarmament crisis: Iraq says it will begin shooting down Lockheed U-2 surveillance planes being used by UNSCOM inspectors.
Severe Tropical Storm Linda devastates southern Vietnam and Thailand, killing 3,275 people.

BBC News 24 has launched a new channel at 5:30pm, after the final closedown with the last national anthem of God Save the Queen, which occurred at approximately 2:57am for BBC One, following the death of Lady Diana Spencer.
Telecom companies WorldCom and MCI Communications announce a US$37 billion merger to form MCI WorldCom, the largest merger in U.S. history.
Mary McAleese is elected the eighth President of Ireland in succession to Mary Robinson, the first time in the world that one woman has succeeded another as elected head of state.
Ramzi Yousef is found guilty of masterminding the 1993 World Trade Center bombing.
In Luxor, Egypt, 62 people are killed by 6 Islamic militants outside the Temple of Hatshepsut.
Metallica released the album Reload internationally.
In Des Moines, Iowa, Bobbi McCaughey gives birth to septuplets in the second known case where all seven babies are born alive, and the first in which all survive infancy.
NASA's Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission is launched, the start of the satellite component of the Clouds and the Earth's Radiant Energy System.
In the Indian state of Bihar, Ranvir Sena attacks the CPI(ML) Party Unity stronghold Lakshmanpur-Bathe, killing 63 lower caste people

In Ottawa (Canada) representatives from 121 countries sign a treaty prohibiting the manufacture and deployment of anti-personnel land mines. However, the United States, the People's Republic of China, Russia, South Korea and 32 other nations do not ratify the treaty.
The capital of Kazakhstan is moved from Almaty to Astana.
The Kyoto Protocol is adopted by a United Nations committee.
Microsoft releases Windows 98 Beta 3.
In Japan, over 700 children suffer photosensitive epilepsy attacks after watching an episode of the Pokémon anime.
Brazil beats Australia 6–0 in the FIFA Confederations Cup final.
50–1010 villagers are killed in the Sid El-Antri massacre in Algeria.
Ulster loyalist paramilitary leader Billy Wright is assassinated inside Long Kesh prison in Northern Ireland.
Hong Kong begins to kill all the chickens within its territory (1.25 million) to stop the spread of a potentially deadly Influenza A virus subtype H5N1 strain.
Wilaya of Relizane massacres of December 30, 1997: In the worst incident in Algeria's insurgency, 423 people from four villages in the wilaya of Relizane are killed.
